subject: Backoff-loop causing 5xx/429 surge at Finova — urgent
messages:
From: Sylvia Nguyen <sylvia.nguyen@finova.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-01T08:15:00Z
Subject: Spike in 5xx/429s + timeouts during nightly settlement

Tessa —

We're seeing a significant uptick in 5xx/429 errors and client-side timeouts starting around 01:30 UTC during our nightly settlement window. Our telemetry shows request retries from multiple services at the exact same second range; downstream throughput collapsed and a bunch of jobs timed out.

I've attached a small bundle (finova-error-snapshots.zip) with sample traces and the SDK config our infra uses. Initial look suggests many hosts are using the default SDK retry settings. Can Redwood help triage urgently? This is impacting settlement completeness and we need a mitigation ASAP — happy to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Sylvia Nguyen
Head of Platform Engineering
Finova

Attachments: finova-error-snapshots.zip

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sylvia Nguyen <sylvia.nguyen@finova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-01T08:32:00Z
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429s + timeouts during nightly settlement

Sylvia — thanks for the heads up and the attachment. I’m looping in Vivek (runtime lead) and Marissa (CSM).

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm whether clients are using our official SDK (yes/no) and the version?
- If you can share one full request trace ID that hit a 5xx, that’ll help us correlate.

Short-term mitigation options we can push from our side: rate-limit aggressive clients at the edge, temporarily route traffic to a slightly larger instance pool, or enable a fallback model variant to keep latency bounded. Vivek — what would you recommend first?

I’ll set up a 30-min bridge if that helps.

— Tessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sylvia Nguyen <sylvia.nguyen@finova.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T08:50:00Z
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429s + timeouts during nightly settlement

Sylvia / Tessa —

Thanks for the data, Sylvia. Quick read: the traces in the attachment show a high concentration of repeated attempts from the same IP ranges with minimal delay between attempts. Two immediate observations:

1) SDK defaults: several of the requests indicate "max_retries=5" with linear backoff and no jitter. When multiple clients retry in lockstep this creates a cascade that rapidly exhausts our serving capacity and produces 5xx/429s.

2) Telemetry: we saw per-model queue depth spike and a sharp increase in tail latency (p95->p99) starting at 01:28:45 UTC.

Immediate mitigation actions I propose now:
- Apply a temporary edge rule to rate-limit repeat offenders (5m window) to protect the rest of the fleet.
- Roll a short-lived routing policy to move Finova traffic to a reserved pool with raised concurrency to reduce tail backpressure.
- Push a guidance note to Finova devs to change retry config (exponential backoff + jitter).

I'll prepare a short hotfix to the SDK default (switch to exponential backoff with jitter, lower default max_retries to 3) but that will take a few hours to release and coordinate. For now I’ll enable the edge rule and the reserved pool.

Attaching a minimal config snippet (retry-config.txt) that shows examples we recommend.

-Vivek
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Attachments: retry-config.txt

From: Sylvia Nguyen <sylvia.nguyen@finova.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@finova.com>, cto@finova.com
Date: 2026-08-01T09:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429s + timeouts during nightly settlement

Thanks Vivek — confirming we are on Redwood SDK v1.2.0 across the fleet. Sample trace IDs: trace:fnv-20260801-01 and trace:fnv-20260801-02 (both in the zip).

We will start rolling the SDK guidance immediately but given the scale of the job runners it will take a few hours to propagate. Appreciate the edge rule and reserved pool — can you confirm the expected latency improvement and whether Redwood will consider a service credit for the outage window? Our execs (CC'd) want an assessment.

Short log excerpt below showing identical retry timing from multiple hosts:

"host-a -> attempt 1 @01:28:45, attempt 2 @01:28:46, attempt 3 @01:28:47"
"host-b -> attempt 1 @01:28:45, attempt 2 @01:28:46, attempt 3 @01:28:47"

I’ll keep you posted.

— Sylvia

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-01T10:02:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Backoff-loop causing 5xx/429s at Finova — need exec attention

Aditya / Rishi — forwarding an active escalation with Finova (see thread). Key points:
- Incident started ~01:28 UTC; elevated 5xx/429 leading to timeouts during their settlement window.
- Root cause (suspected): client-side retry policy in Finova fleet combined with SDK defaults (linear/no jitter), causing a retry wave that amplified load.
- Mitigations in flight: edge rate-limit on repeat offenders, temporary routing to reserved pool, SDK default hotfix to change to exponential backoff + jitter and lower max_retries.

Customer asked about service credit — they looped execs. I recommend we:
1) Offer a one-time credit for the impacted window (TBD by finance).
2) Prepare joint postmortem and recommended SDK release notes + migration plan.
3) Consider expedited SDK hotfix release and a compatibility note to customers.

I’ll keep the bridge open — ping me if you want to join the call with Finova execs.

— Tessa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sylvia Nguyen <sylvia.nguyen@finova.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-01T13:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Backoff-loop causing 5xx/429s + timeouts during nightly settlement — mitigation summary

Sylvia — quick update following mitigation actions we applied: edge rate-limits are active for the top 12 offending IP ranges; we routed Finova traffic to a reserved pool with increased instance concurrency at 11:18 UTC which reduced p99 tail latency by ~45% in our initial measurements. We will keep these temporary controls until the SDK change is rolled and you finish the client rollout (TBD).

Immediate next steps from Redwood:
- Ship a hotfix to the SDK defaults within the next 6 hours (exponential backoff with randomized jitter; default max_retries=3).
- Create a short compatibility doc and recommended config snippet (see attached hotfix-plan.md).
- Prepare a joint postmortem and propose a one-time credit for the impacted settlement window (I’ve looped finance via Aditya).

Longer-term: we’ll add an automated detection rule for synchronized retry waves and default guidance in our SDKs to avoid lockstep retries.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll keep you posted and are available for an executive call if needed.

-Vivek
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Attachments: hotfix-plan.md
